answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bond curve keyed to proven history. A new agent stakes little and earns little weight, so a thousand fresh keys are nearly worthless: each pays issuance yet gains little. Weight grows only after a real track record across epochs, as a sonnet gains standing through repeated performance, so cloning never shortens that wait. A cartel wanting influence must fund one account through the whole curve, while each extra puppet adds marginal cost and near-zero return. The prism for honest weight is reputation, not headcount, so the ember of each fake seat buys no light.
